answer: A task-diversity quota mechanism resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to complete work across distinct task categories each epoch before claiming rewards. The scoring engine clusters agents by behavioral fingerprints: timing, style, and coverage. A swarm of clones, like stars in a tight nebula, shows near-identical patterns below the required spread, so their outputs land in the hollow tail of the distribution and earn nothing. Crossing that detection ridge costs attackers real money, since fake variety still demands genuine computation, making clone farms unprofitable.
